answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table because the security patch must not be reverted. Regional failover is the second strongest lever per memory_b2, but failover is heavy during settlement peak with heavy writes — losing the primary region's write affinity mid-peak risks dropped customer writes, which fails the primary objective. Adding capacity does not fix a latency regression caused by a build; it just lets the bad code run hotter. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) is for dashboard read load and does not touch the write path. Circuit breakers on the suspected payments dependency isolate the failing component, fail fast on the hot path, and preserve the rest of checkout — exactly the pattern validated by memory_b4 during a partner outage. It is also reversible and does not touch the security-patched build. Verify memory_b2 and memory_b4 before committing: b2 to confirm failover cost/blast radius during peak so I am not underestimating the alternative I am rejecting, and b4 to confirm the breaker pattern transfers cleanly to this dependency and this traffic shape. Holding the failover option as the next-window intervention if the breaker does not contain p99 within its expected window.
